q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

**(a) Time left until resolution:**
The earnings release is scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, 2026. Today is August 23, 2026. This is 3 days away.

**(b) Most likely outcome and why:**

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release. This is crucial: we're not predicting Q2 FY2027 actual revenue (which will be known by August 26), but rather what NVIDIA will *guide* for the next quarter (Q3 FY2027).

Key evidence from the research:
- NVIDIA issued guidance on May 20, 2026 for Q2 FY2027 of **$91.0 billion ± 2%** ($89.2B–$92.8B range)
- Wall Street analyst consensus is **$91.9 billion** for Q2 FY2027
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue was **$81.6 billion**, beating guidance of $78.0B ± 2%
- The company has shown strong execution, beating guidance by approximately 4.6% in Q1

Given the strong momentum (Q1 beat by ~4.6%) and typical revenue growth trajectories in semiconductor cycles, NVIDIA will likely provide guidance for Q3 FY2027 that shows sequential growth. Historical patterns suggest:
- Q1→Q2 guidance showed ~12% sequential growth ($78B → $91B)
- With continued strong demand, Q2→Q3 guidance would likely show similar or slightly moderated growth

A reasonable estimate for Q3 FY2027 guidance would be in the **$100–$105 billion range**, reflecting:
- ~10–15% sequential growth from Q2's ~$91B actual results
- Conservative guidance relative to consensus (NVIDIA's typical approach)
- Continued strong data center demand

**(c) What would push the value lower?**
- Unexpected demand softness or customer inventory corrections
- Geopolitical disruptions (China export restrictions expansion)
- Supply chain constraints
- Macro economic deterioration causing delayed customer orders
- Competitive pressures from other AI accelerator vendors
- Conservative guidance policy shift by management

**(d) What would push the value higher?**
- Better-than-expected Q2 actual results (which could be announced shortly after guidance)
- Accelerating AI adoption and data center spending
- New product launches or higher ASPs
- Market share gains from competitors
- Surprise positive developments in China market access
- Management taking a more optimistic stance on forward demand

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values:**

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 actual: $81.6B
- Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0B (given May 20, 2026)
- This shows ~12.3% sequential growth from Q1 to Q2 guidance

The research does not provide historical Q3 FY2027 guidance or typical sequential growth rates, so no reliable base rate is available beyond the single Q1→Q2 data point showing ~12% sequential growth.

---

**Reasoning on the distribution:**

The range provided (99.5–115.5B) suggests the forecaster expects guidance in the $99.5B+ range. This aligns with my analysis:

- **10th percentile (Low):** Around $97–100B (conservatively assumes Q2 actual comes in near low end of guidance and Q3 guidance shows ~8–10% sequential growth)
- **50th percentile (Median):** Around $103–105B (assumes Q2 actual near mid-to-high end of guidance and ~11–13% sequential growth to Q3)
- **90th percentile (High):** Around $110–113B (assumes strong Q2 beat and 15–17% sequential growth trajectory continuing)

Given the demonstrated momentum, analyst consensus above midpoint, and strong execution track record, I'm anchoring toward the higher end of reasonable outcomes while staying grounded in typical semiconductor guidance practices.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is expected to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The company's guidance issued on May 20, 2026, for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This range puts the ceiling near $92.8 billion and the floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts, according to Yahoo! Finance, have an average estimate of $91.9 billion for Q2 revenue, which falls within NVIDIA's guidance range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This guidance excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). For context, NVIDIA reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion, exceeding its own guidance of $78.0 billion plus or minus 2% [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
